// This fixture is the target shape for both rules and must produce zero
// findings. It is named .go.txt rather than _test.go on purpose: the whole-tree
// gate selects `git ls-files -- '*_test.go'`, which matches at any depth, so a
// fixture named _test.go here would be scanned as production test code and the
// violating half of this pair would keep the gate red forever.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

func TestConformingTable(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		want int
	}{
		{name: "one", want: 1},
		{name: "two", want: 2},
	}

	for _, test := range tests {
		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c := qt.New(t)
			c.Assert(test.want, qt.Equals, test.want)
		})
	}
}

func TestConformingHelperTakingT(t *testing.T) {
	assertOne(t)
}

func assertOne(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(1, qt.Equals, 1)
}

// A helper that genuinely belongs to the caller's checker keeps taking a *qt.C.
// There are more than a thousand of these in the tree and neither rule touches
// them.
func assertTwo(c *qt.C) {
	c.Check(2, qt.Equals, 2)
}

func TestConformingHelperTakingC(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	assertTwo(c)
}

// A subtest owns its checker, and a plain closure nested inside that subtest
// uses it. The nested closure is not a subtest and inherits the right checker.
func TestConformingNestedScopes(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("subtest", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)

		check := func() {
			c.Check(3, qt.Equals, 3)
		}
		check()

		t.Run("nested subtest", func(t *testing.T) {
			c := qt.New(t)
			c.Check(4, qt.Equals, 4)
		})
	})
}

// A struct field named c and a composite-literal key named c are the identifier
// c in the syntax tree and neither reads a checker. Reporting either would make
// the borrowed-checker rule fire on ordinary table tests.
func TestConformingFieldNamedC(t *testing.T) {
	type row struct {
		c    int
		want int
	}

	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(1, qt.Equals, 1)

	t.Run("a field named c is not the checker", func(t *testing.T) {
		checker := qt.New(t)
		got := row{c: 5, want: 5}
		checker.Check(got.c, qt.Equals, got.want)
	})
}

// A subtest reads a fixture built by the parent. Only checkers and testing.TBs
// may not cross the boundary; everything else the parent set up may.
func TestConformingSubtestReadsParentFixture(t *testing.T) {
	want := 6

	t.Run("subtest", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)
		c.Check(want, qt.Equals, 6)
	})
}
